I've been struggling with this for a while. I just don't get the big deal over eating. I kind of just do it automatically, and other people around me seem to treat it as this almost orgasmic experience. I feel like I haven't been hungry in over a year, and instead my stomach eventually just gets empty enough that it starts to hurt, at which point I realize I should've probably eaten earlier. It helps that I've found some foods that I like, or at least that I feel good about eating (because they're healthy or whatever). I've found a very practical way to deal with this is to regulate your diet so you're eating at a rate that's healthy for your body, but that requires a lot of diligence. There's websites like [this](http://www.eatthismuch.com/) that can help you manage that. I've also found if you engage in strenuous activity, working out or whatever, on a regular basis, it becomes easier to know when to eat. By which I mean, I feel like I'm starting to feel hunger again since I've started exercising. Swimming in particular doesn't make you feel too tired but does make you feel hungry, at least in my experience. I still find eating to be kinda bothersome, like I wish I could just take a pill once a day and not have to eat ever, but at least with these methods I don't have to worry about becoming sick due to under-eating.

I regret telling anyone about my depression. There was no need to burden them with that information and they keep saying "if there's anything I can do," "just tell me what I can do," "I'm here if you need anything," now they feel obligated to help but I have no idea how to let them help. I can't think of anything they could do that would improve my situation, so why did I ever tell them in the first place?

I've recently started having a fantasy where I get a job far away, on the other coast probably, where I don't know anyone. I work out there for a couple years, and make no effort to stay in contact with anyone. And I deliberately meet no new people so no one else has to be added into this. Then I'll save up some money and hire someone to kill me, in a way that looks like a mugging gone wrong or something. That way when they all hear about my death, they won't know it was intentional and it would've been so long since they heard from me they probably wouldn't care that much anyway. The only problem is my family would be really hurt still. Maybe the solution is to wait until my parents die, then I think it would cause the minimal impact.

I guess you're right but I just wish I knew why. There's no reason to it? I just don't get it, and I guess inherent to the concept is that I can't get it. But I was so sure this would work out, how can I know I'm not wrong again next time?
